# Day 39: Cut an antenna

- Date: Saturday, September 12, 2026
- Block: RF

## Equipment needed

*   Solid core wire and wire cutters
*   SMA jack
*   Tin lid or copper clad board (for a ground plane)
*   NanoVNA

## Prerequisites

*   Day 38 (Calibrated NanoVNA usage).

## Introduction & background

A monopole antenna is simply an open-ended transmission line whose physical length corresponds to a quarter of the wavelength ($\lambda/4$) of the target frequency. When placed over a ground plane, the ground acts as an RF mirror, creating a virtual "image antenna" that completes the other half of a dipole. Because the physical length defines the resonance, tuning an antenna is quite literal: you trim it down until the standing waves align, driving the feedpoint impedance to exactly 50 Ω and producing a deep $S_{11}$ dip on the VNA.

## Core equations

Quarter-wavelength monopole length:
$$L \approx \frac{c}{4f}$$

## Diagram

[Antenna-Theory: Monopole Antenna](http://www.antenna-theory.com/antennas/monopole.php)

## What you're building

1. A physical $\lambda/4$ monopole antenna, intentionally cut too long (~19 cm) for 433 MHz.
2. A ground plane mount using a tin lid and an SMA connector.
3. A documented tuning sequence trimming the wire 5 mm at a time while monitoring the NanoVNA sweep to walk the resonant dip exactly to 433 MHz.

## Activity

Cut a wire to ~19 cm (deliberately long; λ/4 at 433 MHz ≈ 16.4 cm). Mount it on an SMA jack over a small ground plane (a tin lid works). Sweep S11 250–600 MHz; note the dip. Trim 5 mm at a time, photographing the dip walking upward, until it lands on 433 MHz.

## Question to answer

1. Why does the quarter-wave length resonate (what do the standing waves make the feedpoint impedance look like)?
2. What is the ground plane doing (image antenna)?
